sections.title: Letter Jot
paragraphs: The letter (Jot) /jɔt/ sounds mainly like the sound /j/. You hear it in the word (Jahr) /jaːɐ̯/, which means year. This letter has three different sounds in German.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof. Let air flow smoothly while your vocal cords vibrate. For the next sound, push your lips forward slightly. Bring your tongue near the upper gums and voice a smooth buzz. For the last sound, press your tongue behind your upper teeth, then release into that buzz. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In native German words, the letter makes the sound /j/, as in (jung) /jʊŋ/. In words borrowed from French, it makes the sound /ʒ/, as in (Journalist) /ʒʊʁnaˈlɪst/. In loanwords from English, it makes the sound /dʒ/, as in (Job) /dʒɔp/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not read native words with the English sound in jump. Say the sound as in yes instead. Keep your tongue relaxed and do not press it hard against the roof.
